rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Modern humans evolved from an anthropoid ape that left the shrinking Miocene forests for African savannas. Bipedalism came first — Australopithecus walked upright to scan the grass, free its hands and travel far — then hands made stone tools (Homo habilis), tools and hunting rewarded bigger brains, fire (Homo erectus) widened the diet and drove the first migration out of Africa, Neanderthals buried their dead in…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Humans are primates in the family Hominidae. They share an ancestor with living apes. They did not descend from a living chimpanzee.
Australopithecus afarensis, including the fossil called Lucy, was bipedal with a brain near 400 cubic centimetres.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Anthropoid vs hominid:** anthropoids = all higher primates (monkeys + apes + humans); hominids = great apes + humans; hominins = the human branch only.  ·  **Out of Africa (erectus) vs Out of Africa (sapiens):** two expansions — Homo erectus ~1.8 mya; modern sapiens ~60–70 kya.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Evolution of evolvability:** each acquisition (hands, fire, language) increased the species' capacity for further change — culture became the main adaptive engine.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Split ~6–7 mya from a common ape-human ancestor as African forests shrank.  ·  Sequence with drivers: Dryopithecus → Ramapithecus (ground feeding) → Australopithecus (bipedalism, savanna) → H. habilis (tools) → H. erectus (fire, out of Africa) → Neanderthal (burial, cold) → H. sapiens (language, agriculture, global spread).  ·  Four trends: posture, hands, brain/face, culture — with the bipedalism→hands→tools→brain feedback loop.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every non-African human population descends from a small group that left Africa roughly 60,000–70,000 years ago.
